text: The Google November 2026 Core Update started to roll out last Tuesday, November 10th, at around 1 pm ET, and honestly, the chatter around this update has been more muted than most. I suspect that has to do with the third-party Google tracking tools that are struggling to monitor the Google ranking changes. Google is now officially rolling out what it calls the "collapsible sidebar" within Google Search. We spotted this a few weeks ago and we called it then the AI Mode sidebar in Google Search. Robby Stein from Google said "New on the Google desktop homepage globally: we’re rolling out a collapsible sidebar to easily find & jump back into your recent AI searches." Microsoft has just confirmed that it is now shows ads in AI Overviews in Bing Search. We started seeing ads in Bing AI Overviews about three weeks ago, and Microsoft has now confirmed this on the Microsoft Advertising blog. Here is a recap of what happened in the search forums today... Google seems to be placing emojis in the AI-generated "What people are saying" box in Google Search. Google does show emojis in its search results, but these emojis are not coming from the website it is referencing, but rather from Google Search and its AI-generated descriptions. Google seems to be rolling out hotel booking directly on Google in Google Search but through AI Mode. So when you search on Google and Google shows you the hotels, you can now click on a button that says "Continue on Google" and it then takes you through the AI Mode hotel booking feature to book using your Google account. Google Search is testing a new button in the search results named "Show original results." It seems this button does something similar to the "Search instead for" link, where Google will auto correct or adapt your query when it thinks you have a typo in your query or you meant to search for something else. Google has "turned down" its Data Feed validation tool and has removed references to it from the Book actions (Book) structured data help documentation. I am not sure when this tool surfaced but likely sometime between October 2016 and December 2017 alongside the broader Actions on Google developer platform.
